key_verdicts: Simulation Masquerading as Implementation: All 35 directives across telegram_ops.gleam, telegram_creative.gleam, and telegram_collab.gleam return hardcoded static strings claiming actions succeeded without executing any real backend logic.

Critical Mini App Auth Vulnerability: auth.gleam bit_array_to_hex attempts to decode raw 32-byte HMAC bytes as UTF-8, unwrapping failure to empty string. Consequently, validate accepts empty expected_hash and unconditionally rejects all valid non-empty Telegram initData HMAC signatures.

Mini App Freshness & Parser Defects: check_freshness allows arbitrary future auth_date timestamps because it only checks (now - auth_date <= max_age). Query string parsing silently ignores percent-decoding failures and accepts duplicate keys, allowing parameter pollution.

Unauthenticated Mini App HTTP Endpoints: mini_app_routes.route(path) has no authentication parameters, and router.gleam line 3447 invokes it unconditionally upon matching /mini-app/*, exposing sensitive UI views (dashboard, tasks, health, alerts, config) without any Telegram WebApp authentication.

Native Store Candidate Flaws: The OCaml storage candidate in sibling workspace (.uos-workspaces/agy-telegram-admission-20261001) has a non-transactional initialize_new (DDL and meta inserts not wrapped in a single SQLite transaction) and a non-injective request digest (compute_request_digest joins raw key:version:sha without length prefixing or key sanitization, vulnerable to delimiter collision attacks).

Bypassed Ingress Guard: tools/telegram-harness-dispatch directly invokes telegram:handle_message/1, completely bypassing telegram_ingress_guard.gleam allowlist checks and telegram_delivery_ledger.gleam deduplication.

Missing Outbound Rate Limiting & Backoff: telegram_outbound.gleam lacks rate limiting (Telegram enforces 1 msg/sec in private chats, 20/min in groups) and fails to handle HTTP 429 Retry-After responses.

defect_and_gap_analysis.title: Mini App auth.gleam bit_array_to_hex UTF-8 decoding failure
defect_and_gap_analysis.description: In auth.gleam lines 133-149, bit_array_to_hex attempts to decode raw 32-byte HMAC-SHA256 binary output using bit_array.to_string(bits) |> result.unwrap(""). Because cryptographic hashes contain arbitrary non-UTF-8 bytes, bit_array.to_string fails with Error(Nil), which unwraps to an empty string. The subsequent grapheme mapping returns empty string "". In validate(), string.lowercase(computed_hex) == string.lowercase(expected_hash) compares "" against expected_hash. Consequently, all authentic Telegram WebApp HMAC signatures are rejected as InvalidHash, while an attacker providing an empty expected_hash matches "" == "" and passes authentication.
defect_and_gap_analysis.root_cause: Misuse of bit_array.to_string on raw cryptographic hash bytes instead of direct bitwise extraction of 4-bit nibbles or binary pattern matching.
defect_and_gap_analysis.remediation: Replace bit_array_to_hex with pure binary pattern matching: recurse on <<high:4, low:4, rest/bits>> and map each nibble directly to hex characters, with zero UTF-8 conversion. Require independent signed golden test vectors and an empty-hash forgery rejection test.

defect_and_gap_analysis.title: Mini App auth.gleam check_freshness arbitrary future timestamp bypass
defect_and_gap_analysis.description: In auth.gleam lines 181-196, check_freshness checks only (now_unix - auth_date <= max_age_seconds). If an attacker or compromised client provides an auth_date far in the future (e.g. now + 10^7 seconds), now_unix - auth_date is negative, which is mathematically <= max_age_seconds. This allows initData signed with future timestamps to remain valid indefinitely, bypassing replay protection.
defect_and_gap_analysis.root_cause: One-sided freshness bound missing lower-bound clock skew tolerance.
defect_and_gap_analysis.remediation: Enforce bidirectional bounding: (now_unix - auth_date <= max_age_seconds) && (auth_date <= now_unix + clock_skew_tolerance_seconds).

defect_and_gap_analysis.title: Mini App parse_query_string duplicate keys and silent percent-decode fallback
defect_and_gap_analysis.description: parse_query_string splits on & and = then unwraps percent_decode errors by falling back to the raw string. In validate(), list.find picks the first occurrence of hash and user, but data_check_string joins all remaining parameters including duplicates. If an attacker injects duplicate keys or malformed percent-encoded sequences, the HMAC check string diverges from parsed fields.
defect_and_gap_analysis.root_cause: Permissive query string parsing without duplicate key rejection or strict percent-decode error propagation.
defect_and_gap_analysis.remediation: Strictly reject query strings containing duplicate keys or invalid percent-encoding sequences with MalformedData.

defect_and_gap_analysis.title: Unauthenticated Mini App HTTP Endpoints in wisp/router.gleam and mini_app_routes.gleam
defect_and_gap_analysis.description: mini_app_routes.route(path) takes only a path string and has no authentication or session parameter. In router.gleam lines 3444-3448, any request matching mini_app_routes.is_mini_app_path(path) unconditionally invokes html_response(mini_app_routes.route(path)). Any network actor can access /mini-app/dashboard, /mini-app/tasks, /mini-app/health, /mini-app/config, etc., without presenting any Telegram WebApp initData or authentication token.
defect_and_gap_analysis.root_cause: Mini app routes were implemented as static SSR views without connecting to the Telegram auth verification middleware.
defect_and_gap_analysis.remediation: Require Telegram initData or signed session cookie on all protected /mini-app/* routes. Pass validated TelegramUser into route handlers or return HTTP 401 Unauthorized with a login shell.

defect_and_gap_analysis.title: Native Store Non-Transactional initialize_new in telegram_store.ml
defect_and_gap_analysis.description: In telegram_store.ml initialize_new, PRAGMA statements, CREATE TABLE DDLs, and 5 separate INSERT INTO meta queries are executed outside an explicit SQLite transaction (BEGIN IMMEDIATE ... COMMIT). If the process crashes or an error occurs halfway through initialization, a partially initialized, corrupt database file is left on disk.
defect_and_gap_analysis.root_cause: Missing atomic transaction wrapper around multi-statement DDL and metadata initialization.
defect_and_gap_analysis.remediation: Wrap the entire initialization sequence in a single BEGIN IMMEDIATE ... COMMIT block, ensuring automatic rollback on any failure.

defect_and_gap_analysis.title: Native Store Non-Injective compute_request_digest in telegram_store.ml
defect_and_gap_analysis.description: In telegram_store.ml compute_request_digest, read assertions are serialized as: "read:" ^ a.key ^ ":" ^ string_of_int a.expected_version ^ ":" ^ a.expected_sha256 ^ "\n". Because keys and values are joined with colons without length prefixing or character escaping, a key containing colons and newlines (e.g. "foo:0:\nread:bar") produces the exact same serialized digest buffer as two separate assertions for keys "foo" and "bar". This allows hash collision and digest spoofing attacks.
defect_and_gap_analysis.root_cause: Ambiguous delimiter-based serialization of unescaped, variable-length fields.
defect_and_gap_analysis.remediation: Implement strict length-prefixed encoding (e.g. key_len:key:version:sha_len:sha) or formal canonical JSON serialization with unambiguous field delimiters.

defect_and_gap_analysis.title: Bypassed Ingress Guard in tools/telegram-harness-dispatch
defect_and_gap_analysis.description: tools/telegram-harness-dispatch directly invokes telegram:handle_message/1, completely bypassing telegram_ingress_guard.gleam allowlist checks and telegram_delivery_ledger.gleam deduplication. Unauthorized messages dispatched through this CLI wrapper are processed without security filtering.
defect_and_gap_analysis.root_cause: Developer dispatch wrapper wired directly to low-level message router rather than supervised ingress pipeline.
defect_and_gap_analysis.remediation: Rewire telegram-harness-dispatch to route through telegram_ingress_guard:validate_ingress and delivery_ledger before dispatch.

defect_and_gap_analysis.title: Pervasive Simulation in Ops, Creative, and Collab Directives (35 commands)
defect_and_gap_analysis.description: All 35 directives in telegram_ops.gleam (11), telegram_creative.gleam (12), and telegram_collab.gleam (12) return hardcoded static strings claiming successful actions (e.g. key rotation, container resurrection, consensus voting) without executing any real logic or contacting backend services. In telegram_collab.gleam, fabricated claims of cryptographic consensus are returned.
defect_and_gap_analysis.root_cause: Prototype simulation mockups were left in the codebase masquerading as implemented features.
defect_and_gap_analysis.remediation: Explicitly classify all 35 directives as STUB / SIMULATION in user-facing documentation and help text. Replace mock responses with truthful status indicating backend service connectivity requirements, or wire to real underlying services under 2oo3 constitutional consensus.

defect_and_gap_analysis.title: Missing Outbound Rate Limiting & HTTP 429 Retry-After Handling
defect_and_gap_analysis.description: Telegram Bot API imposes strict egress rate limits (1 message/second per private chat, 20 messages/minute per group, ~30 messages/second broadcast). telegram_outbound.gleam sends messages immediately upon invocation without token bucket rate limiting or queueing. When Telegram responds with HTTP 429 Too Many Requests containing a retry_after field, telegram_outbound treats it as a generic HTTP error and fails without backing off.
defect_and_gap_analysis.root_cause: Outbound client lacks a rate-limiting governor and retry state machine.
defect_and_gap_analysis.remediation: Implement a supervised Erlang/Gleam outbound queue with leaky bucket / token bucket rate limiting and automatic exponential backoff honoring Telegram HTTP 429 retry_after headers.
